การอ่านหมายเลขโทรศัพท์ ให้อ่านแบบเรียงตั: Telephone numbers are read digit by digit. Originally, the number 2 was read as โท (tho) so that the sounds of “2” and “3” would be distinct, since telephone numbers consist of many digits and sometimes several 2s and 3s appear in sequence, and the sounds of "2" and "3" are similar. Later, as telephone systems improved greatly and “2” was no longer confused with "3", the digit "2" in telephone numbers came to be read as สอง (song), for example: 0 2225 8622 is read สูน สอง-สอง-สอง-ห้า แปด-หก-สอง-สอง (sun song-song-song-ha paet-hok-song-song)

วันนี้ (1 Mar 17) เวลา 9.30 น. ณ ห้องประ: Today (1 Mar 2017) at 9:30 a.m., in the 5th-floor meeting room of the Office of the Royal Society, the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences held Meeting No. 5/2017, at which Fellows and Associate Fellows presented their research to the Academy and various important matters were considered. The academic lecture on this occasion was on President Xi Jinping's new political theory under the new normal and strict rule of law, by Mr. Sa-nguan Liumanomon, Associate Fellow. The meeting also elected a new Chair and Secretary of the Academy to replace those whose terms were ending
วันนี้ (7 Feb 18) ณ ห้องประชุม 401-403 ม: Today (7 Feb 2018), in Meeting Rooms 401–403, the Academy of Science held Meeting No. 3/2018, chaired by Professor Emeritus Dr. Suraphon Itsarakraisin, M.D., Chair of the Academy of Science. The meeting included an Academy of Science dialogue on “How Can Scientists Help the State Reform Thai Education?” and an academic and research lecture by Professor Emeritus Prida Wibunsawat, Fellow of the Royal Society, on “Liberal Arts and Sciences: The Foundation of Higher Education”. A summary of the lecture will be published later

The meeting summarized preliminary proposals from the sub-meetings of the working group compiling knowledge for national reform of the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences held on Wednesday, 3 and 17 January 2018. เมื่อวันพฤหัสบดีที่ 21 December 2017 ณ ห: On Thursday, 21 December 2017, at Grand Ballroom 1, Maneechan Resort, Chanthaburi Province, at the 13th seminar on the National Memory of the World Register, Mr. Kritsada Bunyasamit, Associate Fellow, Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, and Chair of the Committee for the Revision and Study of Ancient Thai Law, Office of the Royal Society, proposed registering the Three Seals Law as national documentary heritage and Memory of the World documentary heritage in honor of His Majesty King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke the Great, with Professor Sawaeng Bunchaloemwiphat as commentator. The Three Seals Law is a compilation of Thai laws from the Ayutthaya period, which King Rama I ordered to be categorized and revised; it has been in use for over 500 years and shows the historical evolution of Thailand in politics, government, economy, society, arts and culture. As the only existing set, it is irreplaceable and therefore important at both national and global levels

At the center of the sword is an open book bearing the word “ปณฺฑิโต” (pandito), signifying Fellows of the Royal Society whose wisdom is likened to a weapon. Behind the sword and the book are rays radiating all around, signifying the light of wisdom. Below is a ribbon whose two ends curve up to meet the side flaps of the Great Crown. The green of the ribbon is the color of the birthday of His Majesty King Prajadhipok, who graciously established the Royal Society of Thailand on 19 April 1926. Beneath the Great Crown emblem, the words “Office of the Royal Society” curve along the ribbon

๑. คำในภาษาไทยที่ออกเสียงว่า บัน สามารถเ: 1. Thai words pronounced "ban" can be written in several ways, such as บรร, บัน and บรรณ, because each word has a different origin and is formed differently. 2. Words with บรร may come from Khmer, e.g. บรรทม (banthom) from ผทํ; from Sanskrit and Pali, e.g. บรรถร (banthon) from Pali ปตฺถร and Sanskrit ปฺรสฺตร; or may be derived from Thai words, e.g. บรรสาน (bansan) derived from ประสาน (prasan). Learners should consult dictionaries and academic texts on the Thai language and remember the origin or derivation of each word
๑. ชื่อ “ปุณชรัศมิ์” แยกศัพท์ได้เป็นคำว่: 1. The name “ปุณชรัศมิ์” (Punnacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุณ” from Pali “ปุณฺณ”, meaning full - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัศมิ์” from Sanskrit “รศฺมิ”, meaning light. Therefore, “ปุณชรัศมิ์” can be translated as “light born in fullness”. 2. The name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” (Punyacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุญ” from Pali “ปุญฺ?”, meaning merit - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัสมิ์” resembles a word of Pali and Sanskrit origin, but it was not found in Pali or Sanskrit dictionaries. Since not every part of the name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” can be given a meaning, the name as a whole cannot be interpreted
